answers.question: What are the teaching periods at Northstar University?
answers.actual_answer: Northstar University uses Fall, Spring, and Summer teaching periods.

answers.question: What is the normal undergraduate load in Fall or Spring?
answers.actual_answer: The normal undergraduate load is 12–18 credits in Fall or Spring.

retrieved_contexts.text: The normal undergraduate load is 12–18 credits in Fall or Spring and no more than 9 credits in Summer.

answers.question: How much is undergraduate tuition for the 2026-2027 academic year?
answers.actual_answer: Undergraduate tuition for the 2026–2027 academic year is USD 420 per registered credit.

answers.question: How many graded credits must a recipient complete to renew the Northstar Merit Scholarship?
answers.actual_answer: You must complete 12 credits.

retrieved_contexts.text: To renew, a recipient must complete at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term, earn a term GPA of at least 3.30, maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, and have no active serious-conduct sanction.

answers.question: What percentage of scheduled sessions are students expected to attend?
answers.actual_answer: Students must attend 100% of classes and get A grades.

answers.actual_answer: Registration above 18 credits requires a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20 and written approval from the programme director.

answers.question: What happens if I miss an instalment payment on my payment plan?
answers.actual_answer: Missing an instalment creates a financial hold, which blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance.

retrieved_contexts.text: Missing an instalment creates a financial hold.

answers.question: How does a pass/fail course affect my Northstar Merit Scholarship renewal?
answers.actual_answer: Pass/fail courses count toward the credit load only when the student earns a pass, but they do not contribute grade points to the GPA.

retrieved_contexts.text: Pass/fail courses count toward the credit load only when the student earns a pass, but they do not contribute grade points to GPA.

answers.question: Can I take a voluntary leave for employment and reserve my scholarship?
answers.actual_answer: A voluntary leave for employment does not automatically reserve the award; you must request a scholarship deferral before the census date.

retrieved_contexts.text: A voluntary leave for employment or travel does not automatically reserve the award; the student must request a scholarship deferral before the census date.

answers.question: If I disagree with my final grade, who should I contact first and within what timeframe?
answers.actual_answer: You must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published.

retrieved_contexts.text: The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published.

answers.question: Are graduation applications accepted after the census date?
answers.actual_answer: A late application may defer the conferral date even when all academic work is complete. The formal graduation application is due by the census date of the intended graduation term.

retrieved_contexts.text: The formal graduation application is due by the census date of the intended graduation term.

answers.question: If a student drops a course after standard add/drop but before census, and they have the Northstar Merit Scholarship, what happens to their tuition and scholarship?
answers.actual_answer: They receive a 50% tuition reversal. However, dropping below 12 graded credits before or on census triggers an immediate scholarship eligibility review, and scholarship funds are adjusted before any student refund is calculated.

retrieved_contexts.text: From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, 50% is reversed.
Dropping below 12 graded credits on or before the census date triggers an immediate eligibility review.

answers.question: I am an international student and want to withdraw from all my courses to take a medical leave. What steps must I take?

answers.question: Can a student with a pending grade appeal participate in the commencement ceremony?
answers.actual_answer: Participation in a commencement ceremony is ceremonial and is not proof that a degree has been conferred. Students with no more than six credits remaining may request permission to participate early, but a pending grade appeal may delay official conferral.

retrieved_contexts.text: Participation in a commencement ceremony is ceremonial and is not proof that a degree has been conferred.

answers.actual_answer: The late-add fee is USD 40 per course, because Registration Policy version 2.0 (effective August 1, 2026) applies. It must be paid within two business days after approvals.

answers.question: My parent wants to know my conduct information because they pay my tuition. Can the university share this?
answers.actual_answer: No, a parent or sponsor who pays tuition does not automatically receive academic or conduct information. The university may discuss a student's record only with the student or a person who has a valid, recorded authorization.
